tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

All three of us start at the same time. Source of truth is `SPEC.md`; section numbers point into it.
Branch: `jerry/<feature>`. Only edit files you own. Ask in chat before touching anyone else's.

## Hour 0: foundation slice (parallel with Johnny and Hang)

- [ ] **First, within about 10 minutes:** `create-next-app` (TS, App Router, `src/`, Tailwind, ESLint) and pin every §4 dependency exactly. Push to `main`, since everyone else builds on this. While you do it, Johnny and Hang are setting up their accounts.
- [ ] Contracts `src/contracts/{domain,api,gesture,voice,index}.ts` + `fixtures/*`, copied verbatim from §6–§7. Push quickly. Until it lands, the others code against the spec text.
- [ ] `src/components/ui/**`, `app/layout.tsx`, `globals.css`, landing `page.tsx`, `(app)/layout.tsx` nav (Today, Pantry, Recipes, Settings), and empty "TODO (owner)" pages. Use a placeholder `requireUser` until Johnny's auth lands.

# Hang's workstream notes (Workstream C + foundation slice)

Branch: `hang`. Covers `hang.md` Hour 0 + Workstream C tasks 1–10.
Verified: `npm run typecheck` ✓, `npm run lint` (0 errors) ✓, `npm test` (263 pass) ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (with dummy env).

## §17 resolutions (items 1, 2, 3, 10, 15)

- **Item 1 — @google/genai API: RESOLVED by package inspection** (`@google/genai@3.0.0` types).
  `ai.models.generateContent({ model, contents, config })` with `config.tools = [{ googleSearch: {} }]`;
  grounding read from `candidates[0].groundingMetadata` (`groundingChunks[].web`, `webSearchQueries`,
  `searchEntryPoint.renderedContent`). JSON mode via `responseMimeType: 'application/json'` + `responseSchema`,
  images as `{ inlineData: { mimeType, data } }` parts. Implemented in `src/lib/gemini/client.ts`.
  Live proof still needs a key: `GEMINI_API_KEY=... node scripts/gemini-smoke.mjs`.
- **Item 2 — Grounding terms: NOT resolved, needs a human.** I could not read the Gemini API Additional
  Terms from here. Implementation follows the SPEC's cautious default: 24 h discovery-URL cache
  (`recipe_search_cache`), `searchEntryPoint.renderedContent` rendered unmodified in a sandboxed
  `<iframe srcdoc sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox">`. Human: read the terms,
  then keep/shorten/drop the cache.
- **Item 3 — 3.8-flash vs flash-lite: NOT resolved, needs a key.** `GEMINI_SEARCH_MODEL` is
  configurable (`src/lib/env.ts`, default `gemini-3.8-flash`). Human: time 3 discovery runs per model.
- **Item 10 — full step text: team decision needed; default (a) implemented.** Cook/detail views show
  full `HowToStep` text with attribution + always-visible "View original" link. No headnotes/stories
  are ever copied. Human: confirm (a) vs summary-plus-link (b).
- **Item 15 — dev/deploy flags: PARTIALLY resolved.**
  - `next dev --experimental-https` EXISTS in Next 16.4.5 (verified via `next dev --help`), with
    `--experimental-https-key/cert/ca` options. Use it for phone-on-LAN testing.
  - Dockerfile standalone paths match the standard Next 16 output (`.next/standalone/server.js` +
    `.next/static` + `public/`); `npm run build` produces them (verified).
  - sslip.io fallback: unverified here; Caddy auto-TLS against it needs a VPS test.

## Deliberate deviations from SPEC (all marked "tune freely" or forced by tooling)

1. **expiryScore normalization** (`src/server/recipes/score.ts`): SPEC sketches cross-set normalization,
   which forbids streaming each candidate with its final score (F6 step 8). Using per-candidate

Phase 0 resolves items 1–8 before the workstreams fork. Record each answer in this file and in Brain (`entire brain remember`).

| # | Item | Why it matters | How to verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exact `@google/genai` API for (a) grounded search with `googleSearch` and `groundingMetadata`, (b) JSON schema output with images (`interactions.create` vs `models.generateContent`) | The research saw both shapes. The wrapper must work | Read the current SDK README. Run one grounded call and one label-photo call |
| 2 | Gemini **Grounding terms**: must Search Suggestions be displayed, and may grounded results and URLs be cached (24 h search cache, 7-day recipe cache)? | The research could not read the terms page | Read the "Grounding with Google Search" section of the Gemini API Additional Terms. Adjust `recipe_search_cache` TTL or drop it |
| 3 | `gemini-3.8-flash` latency (reported 13.3 s TTFT) vs `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` for discovery. Does Flash-Lite support grounding? | Search UX and the 5k free grounded queries | Time 3 runs of each. Keep `GEMINI_SEARCH_MODEL` configurable |
| 4 | dataandapis not-found shape. Whether misses cost tokens. Units of `sodium` and the carb convention. The team key's plan and quota | Cache policy and correctness | Call with `0000000000000` and with a known product. Check the dashboard token count |
| 5 | OFF v2 field names (`proteins_100g`, `fat_100g`, `_serving`) and not-found shape | Adapter correctness | One staging call (`world.openfoodfacts.net`, basic auth off/off). Save as a fixture |
| 6 | Tiger free service: TimescaleDB present. `WITH (tsdb.hypertable…)` accepts the composite PK. tz-aware `time_bucket` in the cagg. Real-time aggregation. Connection string format. Storage cap (750 MB is third-party) | Migrations | Run the migrations on a fork. `SELECT extname, extversion FROM pg_extension;` |
| 7 | `auth0.getSession()` with no args inside route handlers | Auth on every API route | Quick test route. Fallback to `withApiAuthRequired` |
| 8 | MediaPipe model URL serves. GPU vs CPU delegate on the demo laptop. Laptop FPS | Gesture reliability | Download and commit the model. Enable the dev FPS counter |
| 9 | Exact versions: react, tailwind, zod (does it include `z.fromJSONSchema`, as used in the Gemini docs?), `barcode-detector`, `@google/genai`, `recipe-scrapers` (licence, maintenance), vitest, playwright | Pinning | `npm view <pkg> version license` |
| 10 | Copyright/ToS: is it acceptable to display full `HowToStep` text in cook mode (option a) versus a summary plus link (option b)? | Legal risk. US law treats simple directions as uncopyrightable ([Circular 33](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ33.pdf)), but site ToS and other jurisdictions weren't reviewed | Team decision. Default (a), with attribution and the "View original" link always visible |
| 11 | Allergen enum vs Health Canada's priority allergen list | Completeness of the strict filter | Check Health Canada's list. Adjust `Allergen` (a contract change, §18.5) |
| 12 | ElevenLabs: does the team have a key or credits? Free-tier quota? Is `eleven_v4_turbo` on the team's tier? An earlier report found 3 months free for Canadian students 18+ ([ElevenLabs blog](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/introducing-elevenlabs-for-students)) | Read-aloud quality in the demo | Check the account. The fallback means the demo never depends on it |
| 13 | Entire: is `/session handoff` real? Is `entire blame`/`why` Labs-only? Do Trails or hosted Brain need a paid plan? What is the exact MLH prize wording? | Entire prize proof | `entire --help`, `entire labs`, `entire agent-help`, [pricing](https://entire.com/pricing). Ask the MLH rep |
| 14 | Swipe direction default (right→left = next) and all gesture thresholds | Usability | Hallway test with 3–5 people. Tune `GestureConfig` |
| 15 | `next dev --experimental-https` flag; sslip.io fallback; Dockerfile standalone paths | Dev and deploy | Try them |
| 16 | `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` needed in the CSP for MediaPipe and zxing WASM | CSP | Enable the CSP in staging and watch the console |

**Answers (Jerry, 2026-11-07)**

- **8.** The model URL serves. `public/models/gesture_recognizer.task` is committed (8,373,440 bytes, sha256 `97952348cf6a6a4915c2ea1496b4b37ebabc50cbbf80571435643c455f2b0482`). GPU vs CPU and laptop FPS: *pending a manual test on the demo laptop* (gestures branch).
- **9.** Pinned exactly: `next` 16.4.5, `react`/`react-dom` 19.3.1, `@auth0/nextjs-auth0` 4.33.0, `postgres` 4.1.0, `zod` 4.6.7 (has `z.fromJSONSchema` and `z.toJSONSchema`), `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` 1.2.2, `barcode-detector` 3.2.3 (bundles `zxing-wasm` 3.1.6), `@google/genai` 3.0.0, `recipe-scrapers` 3.5.0 (TypeScript, MIT, last published 2026-10-31), `tailwindcss` 4.3.5 (via `@tailwindcss/turbopack`), `vitest` 5.1.0, `@playwright/test` 1.65.0. Kept create-next-app's `typescript` 5.9.3 and `eslint` 9.39.5 (TS 7 and ESLint 10 exist but weren't adopted), and `@types/node` 22.20.5 to match the Node 22 runtime. **Decision:** create-next-app 16.4.5 enables `cacheComponents` by default; it is **off**, so session reads render dynamically as this spec assumes. `npm run typecheck` runs `next typegen` first, so the global `PageProps`/`LayoutProps` types exist.
- **12.** The team has an ElevenLabs key. Tier and quota are checked when `/api/tts` lands (voice branch).
- **13.** Entire CLI 0.13.1: there is no `/session handoff` (`entire session` has `resume`, `attach`, `adopt`). `entire blame` and `entire why` are Labs commands and available. Trails work on the current plan (trails 1–3 exist). The Brain plugin isn't installed on Jerry's machine (`entire plugin install brain`). The MLH prize wording still needs to be confirmed with the rep.
- **14.** Webcam tests: swipes didn't work, nor did a custom sideways-point detector. **Next/previous are now the built-in ☝️ `Pointing_Up` / 🤟 `ILoveYou`, held 0.8 s with the fingertip still** (§11.1, §11.3). Other thresholds: *pending* further testing.
- **16.** *Pending* until the CSP in `next.config.ts` lands (Hang), then checked in the browser console with hands-free on.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. There are different types of agents that you can launch, with each type having specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Agent types which you are able to launch were given to you in a message from the system at the start of the conversation, and are supplied again if the list of available agents changes.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to choose which type of agent you want to launch. A type of "fork" forks yourself, allowing the fork to inherit your full conversation and context, and ensuring that it runs on the same model that you are running on (a `model` override is ignored for forks). For other types of subagents, they start fresh without your context window. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

The other challenge of subagent usage is that you have less observability into what is happening compared to your own work, where you have full visibility into every single tool call, result, and action that occurs. Subagents run in the background, but you will be notified when one completes. If you don't yet have the results from a subagent that you launched, it is likely still running, so be sure to keep that in mind and not make up results from subagents which haven't yet finished their tasks. The subagent's final report which is given back to you when it has finished is not shown to the user - it is just shown to you, so if you want to relay something from it which is important, you have to do that yourself.

You can use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously-spawned agent with its context still intact, whereas a new Agent call starts fresh (except for fork types, which inherit your context).

Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`). Also take note that `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort.
